questions.prompt: Which gas makes bread dough rise?
questions.explain: Yeast releases carbon dioxide as it ferments sugar.

questions.prompt: Which bacterium turns milk into curd?
questions.explain: Lactobacillus makes lactic acid, which thickens milk.

questions.prompt: In the Fermentation Lab, what happened to dough kept at 60 °C?
options: It didn't rise: the yeast was killed
questions.explain: Yeast is a living fungus; too much heat kills it.

questions.prompt: Why does curd take longer to set in winter?
options: There are no bacteria in winter
The bacteria work more slowly when it's cold
questions.explain: Microbes are slower at low temperatures.

questions.prompt: Plan a fair test to find which temperature makes yeast dough rise the most.
questions.modelAnswer: Make identical dough balls with the same flour, water, sugar and yeast. Put each in a measuring cylinder or a marked jar. Place them at different temperatures (e.g. 10, 25, 35 and 50 °C) using the fridge, the counter and water baths. After 1 hour, measure the height (volume) each dough reached. Keep everything else the same: size of dough, amount of yeast and sugar, time. Repeat three times and compare the averages.
rubric: Control variables: yeast, sugar, dough size, time

questions.prompt: Order the steps to set curd at home.
steps: Stir in a spoonful of curd (the starter)
Cover and leave in a warm place for 5–8 hours
questions.explain: The starter provides the Lactobacillus bacteria.

questions.prompt: Dough had a volume of 200 mL. After rising, it was 320 mL. By what percentage did it rise?
Which foods are made using fermentation by microbes? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Boiled rice is simply cooked, not fermented.
